name: Left Standing
tagline: You'd rather know it's there than have it.
epigraph: The plant behind this glass flowers once in its life. Most are harvested first.
glassware: a copita (a small tulip-shaped tasting glass), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. v4 changes only two pronouns (audit v3 R1, R2). Line that lands: "You start missing things while they're still here." Runner-up: "People sometimes take that for strictness, and you'd rather they did." Also for Robin: "You'd leave the flower where it grows, and a peach is there to be picked." Lint warnings accepted by Wren: "he" (y2) and "his" (y3) are Suro-Piñera, never the guest. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/bat-friendly-agave-suro.md` (*Oxford Companion* AGAVE pdf 74, 77, MARTINI, pdf 600; *Cocktail Codex* pp. 37, 72–73, 86, 88, 164, 174; *Liquid Intelligence* pp. 110, 136–137). Web sources, all secondary and named: *Edible Philly* 2016, *PhillyVoice* 2023, *Mezcalistas* 2024, *Mezcal Reviews* 2022, Univ. of Gothenburg 2024, *Cool Green Science* 2017, batfriendly.org, EDF 2018, BCI 2021, Tequila Matchmaker, SAQ. *Flavor Matrix*: consulted, no agave page, set aside. Room notes: `work/explorer-caregiver/`.
names_note: **Left Standing**, the room's pick (all three, round 7): what this person does with every place they love, and literally true of the agaves nobody harvested. **Left to Flower** is the runner-up, kept for Robin: Tomás's and then Wren's pick while the glass held elderflower; with the peach there's no flower in it, so it only captions the story (Hester). Also considered: *Let Some Flower*, *Once*, *Worth the Waste* (Wren), *You Can Miss It Later*, *The Night Flower* (Tomás). Rejected: *Five Percent*, *Uncut* (*Half a Rim*), *Bat Friendly*, *Leave It* (*Overnight*).
open_items: **Legends and inferences (Hester):** the bats "came back … and found the flowers gone" is our reading of Oxford's migration shift (C5), inside an "I like to think". The peach as "the sweetness the still never got" is romance, signposted.

**Owned conflicts (Hester):** the bat-friendly certification is disputed, and *PhillyVoice* reports "no official certification process" (C1), so the reading says "let some flower", never "certified". Suro-Piñera's bottle is on his own programme's list (C3). There are two bats: only the lesser long-nosed bat recovered (delisted 2018); the Mexican long-nosed bat is still endangered (C7), so nothing says "the bats are back".

**The bottle (Tomás, Hester):** Siembra Azul Blanco (40%, F25) is Suro-Piñera's, but it isn't the bottle on the 2016 bat-friendly list (Siembra Valles Ancestral is: 50%, pit-cooked, smoky, about $120–150). y4 says so in one clause, and nothing says buying it pays for flowers. Any 100% agave blanco of 40% or more is proven in the sweep.

**Crème de pêche and nuts (Tomás):** marked veto-free as his call (made from the fruit). Oxford (pdf 600) says liqueurs were once commonly made from peach kernels; a bottle made with the stones would go to nuts and take the pour off the veto-free floor.
**St-Germain's sugar** was never found (SAQ has no sugar field); it only mattered to the rejected elderflower version.
